angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 35,422,957 km at 79.24 pc = 5.98 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 98337: distance 79.239 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.014), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 79.239 +/- 1.109 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 11.3375 +/- 0.1652 mas (same row, RUWE 8.19), 68.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 50.917 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 98337: radius 50.917 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 559.03 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.065) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 35,422,957 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3936 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 98337: effective temperature 3936 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.093) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 98337: effective temperature 3936 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.093) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * gam Sge: spectral type M0-III (1989ApJS...71..245K)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * gam Sge: projected rotation speed 5.8 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2008AJ....135..209M)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 908) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.06 from 2025A&A...698A..93J; the 21 published values span log g 0.5 to 1.905, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.3% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A%26A...698A..93J)
